children: ZymIQ Technology AB announces that the research project CATCH TB, part of the European Partnership on One Health Antimicrobial Resistance, has been selected for funding. The project has a total budget of EUR 1.65 million over three years. It builds on Mycolyse, the Group’s patent pending technology for enzyme based antibiotics, and will investigate its potential against antibiotic resistant tuberculosis.

Mycolyse is developed by the subsidiary ZymIQ Biopharma. The technology is based on engineered enzymes that attack the protective structures of bacteria. It is intended as a new type of enzyme based antibiotic. The research behind the technology was recently published in the scientific journal Trends in Biotechnology.
The project is coordinated by Lund University and brings together researchers in Sweden, Germany, Portugal and South Africa.
External funding and a basis for partnerships

The project makes it possible to pursue research that is important for Mycolyse with external funding. It also provides access to resistant bacterial strains, specialised models and complementary expertise. Among other things, the project will evaluate efficacy against resistant bacteria, combinations with established antibiotics, and new ways to carry out and improve treatment.
The results will inform decisions on further development and may strengthen discussions with industrial partners and potential licensees.

“Resistant bacteria are one of the greatest threats of our time. The project gives us access to funded research and international expertise that can take Mycolyse forward and open doors to collaborations with pharmaceutical companies,” says Michael Edelborg Christensen, CEO of ZymIQ Technology AB.

“Our enzymes attack the bacteria’s defences. Now we will investigate whether they can help antibiotics work better against resistant tuberculosis. The results will show which candidates we should take forward and how they can best be used,” says Dr. Mats Clarsund, CTO, ZymIQ.
For more details, please see ZymIQ Biopharma’s press release.
The project in brief
Project: CATCH TB (A novel catalytic enabler to enhance antibiotic efficacy against rifampicin and isoniazid resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis)
Focus: Enzyme based treatment strategies against antibiotic resistant tuberculosis
Total project budget: EUR 1.65 million over three years
Programme: European Partnership on One Health Antimicrobial Resistance, EUP OHAMR, Joint Transnational Call 2026
Coordinator: Professor Rajni Hatti Kaul, Lund University
ZymIQ’s role: Industrial development partner through ZymIQ Biopharma
Development stage of Mycolyse: Preclinical
Scientific publication
Abouhmad A. et al. (2026). Engineered phage derived lysins effectively kill mycobacterial pathogens. Trends in Biotechnology.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tibtech.2026.02.015
Contact for questions about Mycolyse and the project
Dr. Mats Clarsund, CTO
ZymIQ Biopharma AB

The final funding of the project is subject to formal approval by each national funding body. Statements about future development and business opportunities are assessments and are conditional on, among other things, positive research results and continued funding.
About ZymIQ Technology

ZymIQ Technology AB is a Swedish life science company based in Lund. The Group develops enzyme based technologies for applications in human and animal health. ZymIQ Biopharma’s development portfolio includes Mycolyse for mycobacterial infections and Stapholyse for staphylococcal infections.
